formula: If n = Sum_j 2^e(j), then a(n) is the XOR of A006017(e(j))'s. Proof: let N+ = XOR and N* denote the nim addition and the nim multiplication, then n N* n = (Sum_j 2^e(j)) N* (Sum_j 2^e(j)) = (Nim-sum_j 2^e(j)) N* (Nim-sum_j 2^e(j)) = (Nim-sum_j (2^e(j) N* 2^e(j))) N+ (Nim-sum_{i<j} ((2^e(i) N* 2^e(j)) N+ (2^e(j) N* 2^e(i)))) = (Nim-sum_j (2^e(j) N* 2^e(j))) N+ (Nim-sum_{i<j} 0) = Nim-sum_j (2^e(j) N* 2^e(j)).
More generally, if n = Sum_j 2^e(j), k is a power of 2, then the nim k-th power of n is the XOR of (nim k-th power of 2^e(j))'s. (End)
